pairs: Mulieris bonæ beatus vir:
Blessed is the husband of a good wife.
numerus enim annorum illius duplex.
For the number of his years is doubled.
Mulier fortis oblectat virum suum,
A good wife delights her husband,
et annos vitæ illius in pace implebit.
and she will fill up the years of his life with peace.
Pars bona mulier bona,
A good wife is a good portion.
in parte timentium Deum dabitur viro pro factis bonis:
She will be given the portion of those who fear God, like a man who has done good deeds.
divitis autem et pauperis cor bonum,
But, rich or poor, with a good heart,
in omni tempore vultus illorum hilaris.
his countenance will be cheerful at all times.
A tribus timuit cor meum,
Of three things, my heart has been afraid,
et in quarto facies mea metuit:
and at a fourth, my face has shown dread:
delaturam civitatis,
an accusation made by a city,
et collectionem populi:
and the gathering of a mob,
calumniam mendacem super mortem omnia gravia:
and a deceitful false accusation. All these are more grievous than death.
dolor cordis et luctus,
A jealous wife is a grief
mulier zelotypa.
and a mourning to the heart.
In muliere zelotypa flagellum linguæ,
In a jealous wife, there is a scourge of the tongue,
omnibus communicans.
which communicates with everyone.
Sicut boum jugum quod movetur,
Like a yoke of oxen being provoked,
ita et mulier nequam:
so also is a wicked wife.
qui tenet illam quasi qui apprehendit scorpionem.
He who has hold of her is like one who has taken hold of a scorpion.
Mulier ebriosa ira magna,
An inebriated wife is a great wrath.
et contumelia:
And her disgrace
et turpitudo illius non tegetur.
and indecency will not be covered.
Fornicatio mulieris in extollentia oculorum,
The fornication of a wife will become known by the haughtiness of her eyes
et in palpebris illius agnoscetur.
and by her eyelids.
In filia non avertente se,
So that her daughter will not also turn away,
firma custodiam,
keep a strict watch; otherwise,
ne inventa occasione utatur se.
having found an opportunity, she may enjoy herself.
Ab omni irreverentia oculorum ejus cave,
Be wary of the irreverence of her eyes,
et ne mireris si te neglexerit.
and you should not wonder if she might disregard you.
Sicut viator sitiens ad fontem os aperiet,
Like a thirsty traveler, she will open her mouth to the fountain,
et ab omni aqua proxima bibet,
and she will drink from every water nearby,
et contra omnem palum sedebit,
and she will sit down beside every fencepost,
et contra omnem sagittam aperiet pharetram donec deficiat.
and she will open her quiver to every arrow, until she becomes weary.
Gratia mulieris sedulæ delectabit virum suum,
The grace of an attentive wife will delight her husband,
et ossa illius impinguabit.
and will fatten his bones.
Disciplina illius datum Dei est.
Her discipline is a gift from God.
Mulier sensata et tacita,
Such is an understanding and quiet wife.
non est immutatio eruditæ animæ.
For there is no substitution for a well-instructed soul.
Gratia super gratiam mulier sancta et pudorata.
A holy and contrite wife is grace upon grace.
Omnis autem ponderatio non est digna continentis animæ.
And no amount of money is equal to the value of a soul with self-restraint.
Sicut sol oriens mundo in altissimis Dei,
Like the sun rising over the world in the high places of God,
sic mulieris bonæ species in ornamentum domus ejus.
so the beauty of a good wife is the adornment of her house.
Lucerna splendens super candelabrum sanctum,
Like a lamp shining atop a holy lampstand,
et species faciei super ætatem stabilem.
so is the beauty of a face in the mature stage of life.
Columnæ aureæ super bases argenteas,
Like golden pillars upon bases of silver,
et pedes firmi super plantas stabilis mulieris.
so are the firm feet of a mature wife upon the soles of her feet.
Fundamenta æterna supra petram solidam,
Like everlasting foundations upon a solid rock,
et mandata Dei in corde mulieris sanctæ.
so are the commandments of God in the heart of a holy wife.
In duobus contristatum est cor meum,
By two things, my heart is greatly saddened,
et in tertio iracundia mihi advenit:
and at a third, anger overwhelms me:
vir bellator deficiens per inopiam;
a man of war failing because of dire need,
et vir sensatus contemptus;
and an understanding man treated with contempt,
et qui transgreditur a justitia ad peccatum:
and anyone who crosses over from justice to sin.
Deus paravit eum ad rhomphæam.
God has prepared such a one for the spear.
Duæ species difficiles et periculosæ mihi apparuerunt:
Two kinds of things have seemed difficult and dangerous to me:
difficile exuitur negotians a negligentia,
a merchant will not be easily freed from his negligence,
et non justificabitur caupo a peccatis labiorum.
and a shopkeeper will not be justified by the sins of his lips.
